definitions.explanation: Used to indicate the first in a series of events, locations, or actions. Almost always appears in the pattern ～を{皮切|かわき}りに (starting with ~).

examples.japanese: {東京|とうきょう}を{皮切|かわき}りに{全国|ぜんこく}ツアーが{始|はじ}まる。
examples.english: The nationwide tour begins starting with Tokyo.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}を{皮切|かわき}りに、{各地|かくち}に{支店|してん}を{出|だ}す{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: Starting with this store, we plan to open branches in various locations.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{成功|せいこう}を{皮切|かわき}りに、{若|わか}い{起業家|きぎょうか}たちが{次々|つぎつぎ}と{新|あたら}しいビジネスを{立|た}ち{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: Starting with his success, young entrepreneurs launched new businesses one after another.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost exclusively used in the pattern ～を{皮切|かわき}りに (starting with ~) or ～を{皮切|かわき}りにして. Rarely used as a standalone noun. This expression implies that a first event triggers or leads to a series of similar events.

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally referred to the first incision ({皮|かわ} = skin, {切|き}り = cut) in moxibustion treatment, which was the most painful. From there, it came to mean the beginning of a series.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～を{皮切|かわき}りに: starting with ~
- ～を{皮切|かわき}りにして: starting with ~ (slightly more formal)
- ～を{皮切|かわき}りとして: starting with ~ (written style)
